text:
maria: CI red on master, failing intermittently: test_rpc_connection_timeout. Seen in 3/5 runs on the same matrix job. Can someone help bisect?
ci-bot: build #9241 failed: https://ci.internal/redwood/9241 — pytest -k test_rpc_connection_timeout · job: linux-x86_64 · logs attached
leo: I can take a look. Do we have the last-green commit for that job?
maria: last green for that pipeline was 1f3a2d9 (merged 2h ago). Bad at head 7b9c4e1.
samuel: suspect PR is #4872 — changed network backoff in rpc/client. Might align with timing.
anya: can you paste the failing traceback? Also try running locally with `PYTHONWARNINGS=error pytest -k test_rpc_connection_timeout -q`
maria: traceback snippet: 
```
E       AssertionError: expected connection to re-establish within 250ms
../tests/test_rpc.py:142: AssertionError
E   TimeoutError: RPC connection exceeded 250ms while waiting for backoff reset
```
leo: thanks. I'm going to run a quick bisect. Proposed range: good=1f3a2d9 bad=7b9c4e1.
devops-bot: reminder: run bisect in CI or locally with `git bisect start <bad> <good>` and `pytest -k test_rpc_connection_timeout` to classify. Use `--runslow` if needed.
leo: starting local bisect now, will post results.
leo: update: after ~14 steps bisect narrowed to commit `a2b1c3f` (merge PR #4872) — test becomes flaky there locally too.
samuel: that matches my suspicion. The backoff change reduced jitter and might cause tight timing windows under load.
maria: can we revert the network backoff change while we investigate? prefer a small revert PR to unblock CI.
leo: drafted revert PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4890 — contains the revert commit and a test tweak to increase timeout to 500ms.
oncall: holding canary deploys for the next 30m. ping me when revert merged.
anya: once revert lands, I'll rerun the flaky matrix a few times and monitor. If stable we can ship a proper fix with more robust retries.
maria: thanks everyone. tagging #postmortems if this recurs. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: rerun queued once revert PR merges.
